prerequisites.title: A Todoist account
prerequisites.detail: The developer platform is free with any Todoist account. Some features depend on the plan of you or the authenticated user.

prerequisites.title: Privacy policy and listing assets
prerequisites.detail: Needed only for certification: marketing description, installation instructions, website and privacy policy links, icon and screenshots.

steps.title: Create the app in the console
steps.detail: Sign in to Todoist, open Settings > Integrations > App Management and add a new integration. Follow the naming and disclaimer rules.
inputs: App name in the form 'X for Todoist'
steps.done_when: The app exists and shows a Client ID and Client secret.

steps.title: Get the Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and add it as the OAuth redirect URL in the Todoist app.
steps.done_when: The redirect URL is saved in the Todoist app.

steps.title: Choose scopes
steps.detail: Pick the smallest set of scopes the agent needs, for example task:add, data:read or data:read_write. Scopes are requested at authorization, not set on the app.
steps.done_when: A scope list is written down, comma-separated.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a custom auth config with your client ID and secret through Composio's API for the todoist toolkit.
steps.done_when: The auth config returns an ID and a test connection succeeds.

steps.title: Prepare demo and listing content
steps.detail: Draft the marketing description, installation instructions and a demo video script showing the integration working as described.
steps.done_when: Drafts are ready for you to review.

steps.title: Record demo and submit for certification
steps.detail: Record the demo video, add icon, screenshots and privacy policy link, then submit the form.

steps.title: Wait for Todoist certification review
steps.detail: Todoist reviews the demo video and may test the integration manually. No duration is published.
steps.done_when: Todoist confirms the listing or reports problems.

traps.title: Token limit can block authorization
traps.detail: If the app exceeds the maximum token limit or is suspended for abuse, users are redirected with invalid_application_status. The limit's value was not found.

traps.title: Naming and disclaimer rules
traps.detail: The app name cannot be 'Todoist' alone, and the description must say it is not created by or affiliated with Todoist. Use of Todoist marks must follow brand guidelines.

traps.title: Multiple redirect URIs require a redirect_uri parameter
traps.detail: If the app has several redirect URIs, authorization requests without redirect_uri are rejected with invalid_request.

traps.title: Older apps may use long-lived tokens
traps.detail: Apps created now issue short-lived access tokens (1 hour) that need refresh. Older tokens stay long-lived until reconnected.

traps.title: Managed app shows Composio name
traps.detail: Under Composio's managed app, consent screens show Composio's name rather than yours, and quota is shared across all Composio users.

blockers.what_it_means: The app exceeded the maximum token limit or was suspended for abuse.
blockers.what_to_do: Check the app in the App Management Console and contact Todoist support.

blockers.what_it_means: A requested scope is unknown or restricted to Todoist first-party use.
blockers.what_to_do: Remove the scope and use documented ones such as data:read or data:read_write.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: This JSON error will be returned to the requester (your user's browser) if redirect URI is not configured in the App Management Console.
evidence.answer: Redirect URIs must be configured in the App Management Console; a request with an unconfigured redirect URI gets a JSON error.

evidence.quote: If your application has multiple redirect URIs configured, this parameter is required — the request will be rejected with invalid_request if it is omitted.
evidence.answer: If an app has multiple redirect URIs configured, the redirect_uri parameter is required in the authorization request.

evidence.answer: Dynamic client registration allows up to 10 redirect URIs, each up to 512 characters, which must be HTTPS (localhost allowed for testing).

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Non-empty array of redirect URIs. Must be HTTPS (localhost allowed for testing).
evidence.answer: For Client ID Metadata Document registration, redirect URIs must be HTTPS (localhost allowed for testing).

evidence.question: G10

evidence.answer: Each registered Todoist app is assigned a unique Client ID and Client Secret needed for the OAuth2 flow.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The unique Client ID of the Todoist application that you registered.
evidence.answer: The Client ID is the unique ID of the registered Todoist application, used in the authorization request.

evidence.question: G10

evidence.answer: Users are redirected to the authorization endpoint with the request parameters, including client_id, scope, state and response_type.

evidence.question: G10

evidence.answer: The scope parameter is a comma-separated list of permissions requested from users.

evidence.answer: Dynamic client registration sends redirect_uris and scope in a POST to the registration endpoint.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: "Todoist" cannot be the primary name of your app.
evidence.answer: The app name cannot be Todoist; it must use a format that signals independence, such as 'x for Todoist' or 'x with Todoist'.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Your application description must state that it is "not created by, affiliated with, or supported by Todoist."
evidence.answer: The app description must state that it is not created by, affiliated with, or supported by Todoist.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Any use of Todoist's marks must comply with our brand guidelines , which are
evidence.answer: Any use of Todoist's marks must comply with Todoist's brand guidelines.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Technical review - We'll review your demo video and, if necessary, manually test the integration to see if it works as described and that there are no critical bugs that prevent users from having a good user experience.
evidence.answer: Certification (optional, for listing) includes a technical review of the developer's demo video, plus manual testing if needed, checking the integration works as described with no critical bugs.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Just add a marketing description, installation instructions, and links to your website and privacy policy.
evidence.answer: The submission form requires a marketing description, installation instructions, website link and privacy policy link, plus an icon and screenshots.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Your privacy policy ensures you will not sell or share our users' data with any third parties without their consent.
evidence.answer: A certification requirement is that the privacy policy ensures the developer will not sell or share users' data with third parties without consent.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Certification isn't required to develop with the Todoist APIs and share the resulting integration with users.
evidence.answer: Certification is optional: developers can build with the Todoist APIs and share integrations with users without passing it; it only affects listing visibility.
